environment: Node 22.14 and PostgreSQL 17.11 using private local fixtures
observations: Wrong checkpoint identity, an accepted pending job and a completed job missing its independent acknowledgement all refused rollover before fencing either endpoint.
Normal worker reconciliation recorded the interrupted completion without a second provider call. The sealed predecessor still recovered through the protected CLI.
The activation CLI verified the retained signed link and switched the same source with an immutable rotation receipt. A wrong successor and a direct source reopening were denied.
The successor accepted and completed a second request. The old receipt remained readable with its original token, and the old observer and worker binding could not act on new work.
Activation could be repeated after new work without changing state. The successor sealed only its own new events, while both sets of source acknowledgements remained present.
The offline tool verified both linked archives. The owner recovered the old archive and its link using public keys after source loss.
scope: The provider was simulated. The source switch, both source and authority databases, observer, app service, worker and owner CLI were exercised locally.
Quarantined replay from a backup across the switch, operation after capacity exhaustion with unfinished jobs and hosted activation remain separate release work.
The optional billing PostgreSQL unit skip is covered by the shared integration suite.
